chapter.title: pybufdump - extensible PyQt event dumper
chapter.para: pybufdump is a Python Qt event dumper. For reference material, see . Features of pybufdump include:

listitem.para: All items are decoded into human readable text.
The ability to only look at a set of selected item types.
The ability to break down event build data into individual event fragments
The ability to assigne textual names to readout source ids.
Support for plugins that can be assigned to do application specific formatting of event builder fragments for specific source ids.
Through use of the python bindings for the unified format library, support for all version of the FRIB/NSCLDAQ data formats supported by that library (currently 10, 11, or 12).
How to operate the program once it is started.
How to associate event source ids with textual names.
How to write plugins to do custom formatting.

section.title: Operating pybufdump
section.para: pybufdump is started via the $DAQBIN/pybufdump command. it is available in FRIB/NSCLDAQ versions 12.2-010 and higher. Several command options control how the dumper operates:

listitem.para: Lets you provde an initial guess about the version of the FRIB/NSCLDAQ data you're looking at. The program will correct this if a ring format item is found in the data.
Allows you to provide a source-id definition file. For more about this, see

Allows you to point to a scaler defintion file of the type used by pyScaler to providee names to scaler channels that are dumped in scaler items. Note that to use this, data sources must be annotated with a sourceid so that the source id associated with each scaler data source is known.
If present, the dumper will treat events as output from the event builder and format the fragments rather than presenting an homogeneous soup of data for physics event.
Using format plugins is only possible with event built data and by enabling this option.

section.para: Once the program has been started, you'll have a window that consists of four segments:

listitem.para: A menu bar at the top which we'll describe below.
A text area that takes up the majority of the window real estate.
A tool bar that currently has one button, a right arrow that advances to the next item in the event file.
A status bar that, when an event file is attached, will show the path to that event file.

section.title: The menus
section.para: This section describes the menus provided by pybufdump. For the most part you will use this to set up the analysis/display of ring items in your source file and then use the right arrow button in the toolbar to advance through the file.
The file menu has the following commands:

listitem.para: Pops up a file selection dialog that allows you to choose the file to dump. If a file is already open, that file is closed first. To prevent confusion, the opened file is listed in the status bar.

Pops up a file selection dialog that allows you to load a python script file that contains a plugin modules. Plugins are described in the
section below.
Requests confirmation and and, if confirmed, exits the program. Window controls will aslo exit the program without confirmation.

section.para: The second menu controls filters. Filters define the set of item types that will be dumpe. All other item types are skipped when encountered in the input file. Initially, all items are dumped. Opening a new event file will not change the filter. The filter menu has the following commands:

listitem.para: Pops up a dialog to select the types to dump. The dialog contains a pair of list boxes. Moving an item type from the left listbox to the right list box adds it to the set of items that will be formatted ( will not be skipped ).
Once the right listbox has the set of item types you want to see, clicking Ok establishes the filter. The filter can be changed at any time.
Goes back to displaying all item types. This is like establishing a filter with all item types in the right box of the filter definition dialog.

section.para: Once you have your event file selected and filters, if any, set up, each click of the right arrow button in the toolbox will advance to the next ring item in the file that is in the filtered list of types and display a formatted version of it.
If you hit the end of the event file the text No more items is displayed and the status bar is blanked out indicating you no longer have an open event file.
Some filters may require some time to get to the next matching item in the event file. Therefore, the cursor takes a busy shape until the next matching item is found.

section.title: Providing a source id definition file
section.para: FRIB/NSCLDAQ ring items can have a source id indicating which data source provided the item. Furthermore, when unpacking event built data anf formatting fragments, each fragment has a source id that, once more, indicates where it came from. Source ids are usually small integer numbers.

The --sourceid-definitions allows you to provide a file that associates text strings with source ids. The format of a source id file is quite simple: Each line of the file defines a text name for a source id. The first columns of each line contain a source id number followed by a space. The rest of the line is the string to associated with that source id.
Below is a sample sourcde id file.

example.title: pybufdump sample source id file
example.programlisting: 0 Event builder output or DDAS crate0 1 DDAS Crate 1 2 DDAS Crate 2

section.para: When a source id definition file is provided, a matching source id will show the text associated with that source id as well as the integer value.
Below, for example, is a begin run item with an annotated source id

informalexample.programlisting:
Begin Run Body header: Timestamp : 0x0000000000000000 Source Id : Event builder output or DDAS crate0 (0) Barrier Type: 0
For run 1196, 0.00 into the run, at Mon 03 Feb 2020 02:57:04 AM Title: good data From original source id: Event builder output or DDAS crate0 (0)

section.title: Writing and loading plugins
section.para: A plugin is a python script that can be dynamically loaded into pybufdump to format some subset of the data in a physics event ring item. This section describes what plugins do, in a bit more detail, how to write a plugin and register its formatters with pybufdump as well as some of the services that pybufdump provides to plugins.

A plugin can provide custom formatting to event fragments in event built data that match specific source ids. Using a plugin, therefore requires that pybufdump have been run with the --unpack-fragments option.
Plugins must, in general:

listitem.para: Provide one more classes that implement a format method. Such classes are called formatting classes or formatter
Provide an unbound function named registerFormatter that registers instances of the formatting classes defined in the plugin to format data from fragments that have specific source ids.

section.para: It's worth noting here that a sample formatter, that formats fragments with XIA/DDAS data in FRIB/NSCLDAQ foramt for version 11 is provided in $DAQSHARE/pydumper/samplePlugin.py. I recommend looking at this code before attempting to write your own plugin.

Let's now start by looking at formatting classes. The only requirement of these classes is that they provide and implement a method of the following type (we use Python 3 type hints here for clarity):

The parameters of this method are the source id of the fragment that is to be formatted, and the body of the fragment. Note that in general, this body in cludes a ring item header and a body header. As the type signature indicates, the body is passed as a byte array. Normally the struct module's unpack can be used to get data from this byte array or, rather slices of it.
The expectation is that the formatter will return a string. The pybufdump program will use this string as the formatted body of the fragment.

Formatter's must be associated with source id of fragments. This is done by the plugin providing a function that must be called registerFormatters that is passed an object that is the pybufdump controller. It's not so important to know wha the controller does, in the design of the pybufdump program, only the services it provides.
Below is the registerformatters function from the sample plugin provided in $DAQSHARE/pydumper/samplePlugin.py.

example.title: Sample registerFormatters pydumper plugin function
example.programlisting:
ddas_sources : list[int] = [0, 2, 3] ...
def registerFormatters(controller : object) -> None: ''' After our plugin is loaded, this function is called and must register instances of DDASFormatter for each source id we're going to provide: ''' for src in ddas_sources: formatter = DDAS11Formatter(controller) controller.registerFormatter(src, formatter)

section.para: As you can see, for each sourcde id in the ddas_sources variable, it creates an instance of the DDAS11Formatter and invokes registerFormatter on the controller it was passed to associate that formatter with that source id.
So that the formatter can make use of controller formatting helper functions, the controller is passed to the constructor of our formatter.

section.title: Controller services for plugins..
section.para: The pybufdump controller provides several servicdes for plugins. This section provides reference material for those methods.

listitem.para: Registers an instance of a formatter, object to format data from fragments that came from the source identified by srcid. This replaces any existing formatter for that source id that might already exist.
Returns a string that formats data as a set of unsigned 16 bit words in hexadecimal format.

Assumes the body is the ring item body of event built data, this returns a string that data. If the sourceid of a fragment matches the registration of a plugin, that plugin is allowed to format the body of the fragment. If not, formatByteArray is used to format the fragment instead.
This method is intended to support plugins for data from events built in a multi-level event builder.
Returns a textual string for a source id. If a source id definition file has been specified, it is consulted to format the string.
